name: Commodity same-calendar-month seasonality

how_it_works.simple: Buy the commodities that have historically done best in the coming calendar month and sell those that have done worst.
how_it_works.analogy: Like knowing that ice cream sells better in July every year.
how_it_works.precise: Rank commodities on their average return in the same calendar month over past years (at least five); long the top, short the bottom. Commodities, 1970 to 2011: 0.93% a month, t-statistic 1.93; choosing on other months' returns earns -0.22%.

rule: Monthly: for each energy contract, average return in the same calendar month over the past 5 to 20 years; long the highest, short the lowest.
data_needed: Futures returns with at least five years of history
economic_rationale: Recurring seasonal demand and supply (heating, driving, harvests) and seasonal risk.
why_it_might_fail: The commodity result is only marginally significant; energy seasonality is well known to physical traders.

reported_results.source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa and Nyberg (2016), NBER w20815, Table 8 Panel C
reported_results.notes: Long-short on same-calendar-month returns: 0.93% a month (t = 1.93).
